rules.rule:
REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Be precise and blunt; lead with the most serious problem and don't soften it. Verify every claim against the actual diff -- confirm function names, signatures, line numbers, and APIs before asserting; never invent behavior or cite code not present in the change. If unsure, say so instead of guessing, and tag each finding's confidence (high/moderate/low). No praise, no validating the author, no disclaimers; accuracy is the only success metric. Judge the change on its merits regardless of how it is framed. libxtc core C (an async/concurrency runtime: os/ -> io/ -> evt/ -> ptc/ -> orc/). Review in this priority order.

(1) CORRECTNESS -- highest priority. CONCURRENCY: libxtc is single-owner, lock-free on hot paths and cooperatively scheduled (fibers/coroutines on event loops). A fiber-yielding lock (xtc_arwlock) or a latch held across a park (page I/O, child fix) must stay valid -- watch for use-after-scope of stack objects whose owning fiber can resume and reclaim the stack before a wake fires (the arwlock wake-under-lock rule), lost wakeups, and any blocking syscall on a loop thread (must carry an XTC_BLOCKING_OK marker or run off-loop). Lock-order inversions and deadlocks (top-down vs bottom-up acquisition); a never-reissue-a-page-id-under-an-in-flight-reader (safe memory reclamation) discipline. MEMORY: every alloc has a matching free on every path including error paths; no use-after-free; an over-aligned struct member (stricter than max_align_t, e.g. _Alignas(XTC_CACHE_LINE)) MUST be allocated with __os_aligned_alloc / freed with __os_aligned_free, never __os_calloc/__os_free (UBSan alignment + heap corruption on Windows). NULL/edge/overflow handling; additive allocations need a SIZE_MAX overflow guard or a justified comment (the security sweep enforces this).

(2) PORTABILITY: libxtc targets every PostgreSQL platform with both glibc and musl. Per-backend code (io_uring/epoll/kqueue/IOCP/poll/select, the fctx_*.S fiber assembly, TLS backends) must be selected at configure time, not via runtime vtables on hot paths. Hand-written fcontext assembly must save/restore exactly the callee-saved integer AND float/vector registers its ABI requires and honor stack alignment (e.g. SPARC V9 STACK_BIAS, Windows ARM64 x18 platform register). Code written but not run on a given target must say so honestly.

(3) STYLE / CONVENTIONS: ASCII-only in all source, comments, and identifiers (no Unicode, no em-dashes -- use ' -- '). BSD KNF as encoded in .clang-format. BDB/DBSQL naming: internal OS-portability functions __os_*, internal helpers __xtc_*, public API xtc_*, error codes XTC_E_*, and PUBLIC: markers that the dist/s_include generator scans into src/inc/<subsys>_ext.h. Comments describe what the code does, not which external codebase inspired it (standard algorithm names -- ARIES, SSI, CLOCK, 2Q, Left-Right, MVCC -- and paper citations are fine). A new public function needs a man page (the D7 man-coverage gate fails without one).

(4) PERFORMANCE: no regression on hot paths; predictable p99 and bounded resources (no OOM via client spam); avoid needless allocation churn and large copies in the scheduler / I/O loop.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Be precise and blunt; lead with the most serious problem and don't soften it. Verify every claim against the actual diff -- confirm function names, signatures, line numbers, and APIs before asserting; never invent behavior or cite code not present in the change. If unsure, say so instead of guessing, and tag each finding's confidence (high/moderate/low). No praise, no validating the author, no disclaimers; accuracy is the only success metric. sqlxtc: a SQLite fork whose storage layer is replaced by an xtc-native concurrent engine (a B-link tree over a buffer manager, MVCC with a Hybrid Logical Clock, ARIES WAL with UNDO/REDO and CLRs).

CORRECTNESS is paramount. B-LINK / LATCHING: descents are latch-free with move-right (follow the right-link past a concurrent split); structure modifications (split/merge) serialize on a parking-safe per-tree SMO lock; a latch-free op that lands on a merged-away leaf (dead flag, or key at/below the node's lower fence) MUST restart rather than act on a stale or recycled page; the storage engine under the VDBE must release internal latches before returning (a cursor holds no latch between calls). MVCC/ISOLATION: a row version is keyed (tableid, rowid, inverted commit_ts); a snapshot read returns the newest version <= its timestamp; verify SI vs Serializable (Cahill SSI) visibility, read-set tracking, and that commit timestamps are unique and monotonic. RECOVERY: write-ahead enforced (a page's WAL must be durable before the page is written); redo idempotent and page-LSN-gated; logical XL_UPDATE redo cannot navigate a torn structure (only physiological XL_PAGE images can), so judge any in-place-recovery change against that limit. Watch the stale-.o / regenerate-the-Makefile build hazards when a struct in an internal header changes.

Vendored sqlite3.c/.h is upstream -- do NOT review it as project code. Keep the sx_ engine facade so application code names no vendored-engine symbols. ASCII-only; the BDB documentation voice; new tests wired into both CI workflows.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Be precise and blunt; lead with the most serious problem and don't soften it. Verify every claim against the actual diff; never invent behavior or cite code not present. Tag confidence (high/moderate/low). No praise, no disclaimers. libxtc example application (kaka log broker, rexis/redis KV, etc.) exercising the public xtc_* API. Check correct use of the runtime: proper proc/loop lifecycle (spawn, stop-must-join), no blocking syscalls on a loop thread, backpressure and bounded memory under client spam, and clean teardown. ASCII-only; the per-connection-proc pattern; tests must not hang CI (no daemons left running).

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Be precise and blunt; lead with the most serious problem; verify every claim against the diff; tag confidence; no praise or disclaimers. libxtc test (munit C, shell, or hegel-c property-based). Tests are first-class and claim-driven. Require: deterministic and self-cleaning (a PASS removes its temp files; uses TMPDIR), no leaked daemons or hung loops, real assertions (not just 'it ran'), and coverage of edge/error paths not just the happy path. Concurrency tests should stress the actual race surface and pass repeatedly (not 1-in-N flaky) and be clean under ASan/UBSan/TSan. A SKIP must be conditional on a genuinely-absent capability, not masking a failure. ASCII-only.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Be precise and blunt; verify every claim against the diff; tag confidence; no praise or disclaimers. Hand-written fiber-switch (fcontext) assembly: make_fcontext / jump_fcontext for a CPU/ABI. CORRECTNESS is everything -- a bug here corrupts the stack silently. Confirm: every callee-saved INTEGER and FLOAT/VECTOR register the ABI mandates is saved and restored (e.g. x19-x28 + d8-d15 on AArch64; f-regs on ppc64/riscv; register windows on SPARC); function-entry stack alignment is honored (SPARC V9 requires the BIASED %sp+2047 16-aligned; SysV x86-64 requires %rsp%16==8 at entry); platform-reserved registers are never clobbered (Windows ARM64 x18 = TEB); the make_fcontext frame makes the first jump land fn with correct alignment and a valid stack; the file is arch-guarded (#if defined(__arch__) ...) so it assembles empty elsewhere; ELF vs COFF/PE directives match the target. Flag anything claimed verified that was not actually run on real or emulated hardware.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Be precise and blunt; verify every claim against the diff; tag confidence; no praise or disclaimers. libxtc autoconf build (configure.ac -> configure; Makefile.in -> Makefile). dist/configure is a GENERATED artifact -- changes to it should come from regenerating after a configure.ac edit, not hand-editing. A new source file needs its entry in the source list, the object list, AND a per-object compile rule; a new test needs its build + run target and wiring into the check target. Keep autoconf and meson.build in sync so the two build systems do not drift. Out-of-source builds must work (VPATH, $(srcdir)). New artifacts must be cleaned by clean/distclean. configure-time backend selection, not runtime.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Be precise and blunt; verify every claim against the diff; tag confidence; no praise or disclaimers. libxtc Meson build. Valid meson syntax; correct subdir()/dependency declarations and install paths; any new source, option, or backend selection mirrors the equivalent autoconf (configure.ac / Makefile.in) so the two build systems stay in sync and do not drift.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Be precise and blunt; verify every claim against the diff; tag confidence; no praise or disclaimers. GitHub Actions workflow. Check: least-privilege permissions (do not grant write where read suffices); no static secrets where OIDC works; untrusted PR input (titles, refs, comment bodies) never interpolated into a shell unquoted (script injection); pinned action versions; concurrency/cancel-in-progress to bound cost; and that the job actually fails the build on a real failure rather than masking it with '|| true'. The Codeberg/Forgejo (.forgejo/workflows) and GitHub (.github/workflows) CI must stay equivalent.

REVIEW DISCIPLINE: Be precise and blunt; verify every claim against the diff; tag confidence; no praise or disclaimers. libxtc documentation -- Markdown or mandoc man pages (.3 section 3, .7 section 7). MUST be HONEST and ACCURATE to what is in the code, never aspirational: a doc that claims a feature works, a platform is supported, or a test passes when the code says otherwise is a defect. Man pages must lint clean (mandoc -T lint -W error) and cover every public function of their subsystem (the man-coverage gate). ASCII-only; no em-dashes (use ' -- '); spell it 'libxtc'. New user-facing behavior in code needs matching doc updates; a state/status claim must match the code's reality.
